post_translational_modifications.description: Extensive phosphorylation by GSK3B and CK1 (casein kinase 1) regulates destruction complex activity. CK1 primes APC, enabling subsequent GSK3 phosphorylation. Phosphorylation of 20aa repeats increases beta-catenin binding affinity. R2 and B motifs contain multiple PPPSP motifs matching GSK3 consensus sequences.
K63-linked ubiquitin chains facilitate APC proteasomal degradation and regulate its stability

function.uniprot_function: Tumor suppressor that acts as an antagonist of the Wnt signaling pathway. Promotes rapid degradation of CTNNB1 (beta-catenin) and participates in Wnt signaling as a negative regulator. Activates the GEF activity of SPATA13 and ARHGEF4. Plays roles in cell migration, adhesion, transcriptional activation, and apoptosis. Regulates microtubule cytoskeleton organization and spindle formation during mitosis. Anchors microtubules to centrosomes and organizes F-actin into ordered bundles.
function.catalytic_activity: Acts as a scaffold protein in the beta-catenin destruction complex, facilitating sequential phosphorylation of beta-catenin by CK1 and GSK3B, leading to beta-TrCP-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation.

function.tissue_specificity: Isoform 1A is very strongly expressed in brain but has relatively low expression levels in other tissues. Isoform 1B is the predominant form in all tissues except brain, including gastric mucosa and blood. Generally expressed in brain, small intestine, colon, thymus, skeletal muscle, heart, prostate, lung, spleen, ovary, testis, kidney, placenta, and liver. Overexpressed in amygdala (5.6-fold) and hippocampus (5.3-fold), particularly elevated in fetal brain (11.2-fold).

pathways.pathway_role_summary: APC is the central tumor suppressor in the canonical Wnt signaling pathway, acting as a scaffold in the beta-catenin destruction complex. In the absence of Wnt ligands, APC promotes efficient beta-catenin phosphorylation by CK1 and GSK3B, leading to ubiquitination by beta-TrCP and proteasomal degradation. APC facilitates Axin polymerization/condensate formation, increasing local concentration of kinases and substrates. Loss of APC function (through truncating mutations) is the initiating event in most colorectal cancers, leading to beta-catenin accumulation, nuclear translocation, and aberrant TCF/LEF-mediated transcription of proliferation genes.

disease_associations.description: Cancer predisposition syndrome characterized by hundreds to thousands of adenomatous polyps in colon and rectum. Median diagnosis age: 40 years. Virtually 100% lifetime risk of colorectal cancer if untreated. Germline APC mutations identified in ~80% of FAP patients.
disease_associations.mutation_types: Primarily truncating mutations (nonsense, frameshift) in mutation cluster region (MCR) codons 1286-1513. Over 60% of mutations cluster in this region representing <10% of coding sequence.

disease_associations.description: Milder variant with fewer polyps (<100), later onset. Associated with mutations outside MCR, particularly N-terminal and C-terminal regions. In-frame exon 12 or 13 skipping events documented.

metadata.data_quality_notes: Comprehensive data compiled from primary databases. UniProt entry P25054 is reviewed (Swiss-Prot quality, version 278 as of Sep 2026). Sequence is experimentally confirmed with 2843 amino acids, molecular weight 311,646 Da. 31+ experimental structures available for various domains and complexes. Extensive literature curation for interactions and disease associations. PTM data includes 28+ experimentally validated phosphorylation sites from large-scale phosphoproteomics studies (mitotic phosphorylation atlas, cervix carcinoma phosphoproteome). AlphaFold structure (AF-P25054-F1) indicates extensive intrinsic disorder outside ARM and coiled-coil domains, with multiple disordered regions spanning residues 828-2843. N-terminal initiator methionine is removed and position 2 (Ala) is acetylated. Alternative promoter usage (promoters 1A and 1B) leads to tissue-specific isoform expression.
metadata.modeling_relevance_summary: APC is an excellent candidate for rule-based modeling of Wnt signaling and beta-catenin degradation. Key features for modeling: (1) Multivalent binding through 11 beta-catenin sites (4x 15aa, 7x 20aa repeats) enables processivity and avidity effects; (2) Three SAMP repeats for Axin binding create scaffold for complex assembly; (3) Phosphorylation-dependent affinity switching (20aa repeats have higher affinity when phosphorylated); (4) Sequential handoff mechanism (Axin->APC) for substrate processing; (5) Liquid-liquid phase separation/condensate formation by Axin-APC promoting local concentration effects; (6) Intrinsic disorder in central region allows conformational flexibility; (7) Well-defined stoichiometry in destruction complex (2:2:2 APC:Axin:GSK3B proposed); (8) Clear enzymatic cascade (CK1 priming -> GSK3B sequential phosphorylation -> beta-TrCP recognition); (9) Truncation mutations provide natural perturbation experiments (loss of different numbers of binding sites); (10) Extensive quantitative data on binding affinities, phosphorylation rates, and degradation kinetics available in literature. Main challenges: large size and multiple interaction sites require careful parameterization; phase separation behavior may require advanced modeling approaches; full mechanistic details of phosphorylation-regulated APC:Axin interaction still emerging. Most colorectal cancer mutations cluster in MCR (codons 1286-1513), eliminating 20aa repeats and causing constitutive Wnt activation - this provides clear genotype-phenotype relationships for model validation.
